title: heterogeneous-capacity-priming-sprintboard-2026-05-20
content:
Sprintboard notes — heterogeneous capacity priming (Wed 2026-05-20)

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (owner)
- Diego Alvarez
- Priya Nair
- Samir Patel
- Ella Johansson
- Joined for 10m: Ayesha (SRE) and Oli (Solutions eng)

Purpose:
Quick sync to capture results from this week's priming experiment (mixed GPU pool: H100 + A100 + L4), decide short-term config tweaks, and capture next actions for the regional surge dry-run next Tuesday. This doc is a working scratchpad — rough notes + TODOs.

High-level summary / takeaways:
- Priming windows (2x 30m in us-west1, 1x 30m in eu-west1) meaningfully reduced first-token latency for cold model copies on H100 by ~42% (p50) and ~33% (p95) vs baseline cold starts.
- L4-backed instances show much smaller cold-start gains (10–12%), likely because quantized model blobs load faster but have slower warm inference throughput.
- Preemption on spot-like machines caused ~4% request failures during the second us-west1 window when we pushed higher concurrency; failure correlated with a worker eviction spike from the cloud provider.
- Cost impact: short-term priming increased cloud spend for the window by ~6% but reduced token-cost-per-second for high-QPS routes by an estimated 8% over the measurement horizon (48h).

Detailed observations:
1) Telemetry snapshot (aggregate during windows):
   - us-west1 window A (H100-heavy): avg GPU utilization 72% -> 85% during warm-only period; queue latency drop p50 from 85ms -> 13ms for cold requests; model load time median 2.1s -> 0.9s.
   - us-west1 window B (mixed A100/H100/L4): observed cross-GPU scheduling jitter — 7% of requests got routed to slower L4 nodes due to early-round robin because of scheduler timing.
   - eu-west1 window (A100-focused): utilization gains smaller; queue latency p95 improved 24% but absolute p95 still ~420ms due to steady background traffic.

2) Failure and preemption notes:
   - Preemption spike at 2026-05-20T14:12Z in us-west1: 18 nodes preempted over 3m. Canary fallback fired, but 12 requests failed with 429 / transient-500 during failover.
   - Root cause: provider-side preemption policy abrupt change + our eviction-drain timeout set to 45s (too short to gracefully checkpoint KV-cache).
   - Short-term mitigation: increase drain timeout to 90s for priming pools; SRE to open provider ticket and request preemption window telemetry. (See JIRA-INF-4821)

3) Scheduling and routing behavior:
   - Scheduler currently uses size-based packing which incorrectly treated L4 nodes as equivalent for initial placement. Need a policy tweak: prefer H100/A100 for routes with >1.2s expected model load.
   - Proposal: add route-level hardware affinity tag (low-effort) and a scheduler pass that respects a hardware-weighted score. Prototype PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priming-scripts/pull/67

4) Cost simulation quick math (48h window):
   - Extra priming runtime: +$3.8k (one-off during priming windows)
   - Estimated token-cost savings for high-QPS endpoints: ~$6.2k (reduced retry & latency-related overhead); net delta = -$2.4k (priming pays off over short horizon for heavy routes).
   - For low-traffic routes priming is neutral/negative. Recommendation: only enable aggressive priming for routes tagged as "hot" (QPS > 20 sustained).

Decisions made during sync:
- Enable 30m priming windows for hot routes in us-west1 and eu-west1 for next 3 business days. (Owner: Maya)
- Increase eviction-drain timeout to 90s for priming pools; add a 2m graceful checkpoint attempt for KV-cache before forced kill. (Owner: Ayesha / SRE)
- Scheduler change to respect hardware affinity tags: implement a lightweight scoring pass in the next sprint; follow-up PR from Diego. (Owner: Diego)
- Add metric that tracks percent of requests served by L4 for routes that have hardware affinity set; alert if >5%. (Owner: Priya)

Action items (explicit):
- Maya: create canary config and rollout plan for toggling priming on/off per-route; link Confluence page (by 2026-05-22). Linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/heterogeneous-fleet-primer
- Diego: open scheduler PR to add hardware-weighted scoring and hardware-affinity tags (due 2026-05-27). Linked PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/203
- Ayesha: provider ticket + request preemption telemetry; update JIRA-INF-4821 with provider response (due 2026-05-21).
- Priya: implement L4-usage metric and set alert in Grafana; add dashboard panel for priming vs baseline (due 2026-05-24).
- Samir: run a 1h dry-run next Tue (2026-05-26) simulating 2x normal surge; coordinate with Solutions Eng to notify customers that might be impacted (due 2026-05-25).
- Ella: draft runbook blurb for priming flip + rollback steps for oncall (due 2026-05-21).

Open questions / risks:
- Is the 90s drain enough to avoid KV-cache corruption on larger models (32B+)? We saw partial state loss in one sample — needs deeper test.
- Spot/Preemptible volatility: do we mark priming pools as non-preemptible (reserved) for critical regions? Cost vs reliability tradeoff analysis needed.
- Scheduler complexity: adding hardware affinity increases placement constraints — could reduce overall packing efficiency. Need a simulation run to quantify.

Experiment ideas (backlog):
- Multi-phase priming: short (10m) + long (30m) windows to test diminishing returns and compute marginal benefit curve.
- Predictive priming using recent QPS trend: kick priming when 10-min moving average crosses threshold (prototype in Python ready, Samir to test).
- Preemption-resilient priming: have lightweight checkpoint persist to S3 every 20s during priming to permit faster warm-up recovery.
